description: Operator-over-proposition layer: MODALITY (graded truth gating entailment — only fact/necessary chain), NEGATION-SCOPE (which constituent the NOT dominates), ToM (a believes operator scoping a nested sub-model that can diverge from reality), GIVEN/NEW (definite=given/refer, indefinite=new/mint). Modality, negation and the belief operator are one wrapper at different scopes.

microtheory.name: modality_tom
microtheory.description: modality/negation operators + theory of mind + given/new

attrs.name: modality
attrs.description: An OPERATOR node over a proposition (structurally like the figurative wrapper and like NOT): it stamps the proposition truth-status as graded possibility/necessity/obligation (a Beta-style value, not flat assertion), so the inference engine refuses to forward-chain a "might" as fact. epistemic might/could = possible; must/will = necessary; deontic should/must = obligation. Only fact/necessary propositions are entailed.

attrs.name: negation_scope
attrs.description: NEGATION is an operator; its SCOPE is which subgraph the NOT dominates, resolved by the same constituent/c-command structure used to attach roles. "I did not say he stole it" lands the negation on a different constituent (say / he / stole / it) for each reading — the focus IS the meaning.

attrs.name: theory_of_mind
attrs.description: A NESTED situation model: a belief-frame attributed to another agent under a believes operator — the sibling of modality, an operator scoping a whole sub-model rather than one proposition. The attributed belief can DIVERGE from world-state (false belief): you answer from the agent belief-model, not reality (Sally-Anne).

attrs.name: given_new
attrs.description: Purely the referent-resolution definiteness branch: definite "the X" refers_to an existing Concept (GIVEN), indefinite "a X" mints a new node (NEW) — the same get-or-create dedup as the slang canonical-concept wiring; drives article choice + anaphora.
